title_en: Shandong Denghai Xianfeng Seed Industry Co., Ltd. v. Shaanxi Nongfeng Seed Co., Ltd. and Shanxi Dafeng Seed Co., Ltd. — dispute over infringement of new plant variety rights
ruling_gist_en: Determining that the characteristics and traits of the alleged infringing reproductive material are identical to those of the authorized variety is a prerequisite for finding infringement of a new plant variety right. When a DNA fingerprinting test concludes that the two are identical or similar, but a field planting DUS test determines that the two have clear and reproducible differences, and the distinctness conclusion differs from the DNA fingerprinting test conclusion, the field planting DUS test conclusion shall be used to determine that no infringement of the new plant variety right has occurred.

full_text_en:
Shandong Denghai Pioneer Seed Co., Ltd. v. Shaanxi Nongfeng Seed Co., Ltd. and Shanxi Dafeng Seed Co., Ltd. — dispute over infringement of new plant variety rights

Ruling Summary

Determining that the characteristics and traits of the alleged infringing propagation material are identical to those of the authorized variety is a prerequisite for finding infringement of new plant variety rights. When the conclusion of DNA fingerprint testing is that the two are identical or similar, but DUS testing through field planting determines that there are obvious and reproducible differences between them, and the specificity conclusion differs from the DNA fingerprint testing conclusion, the DUS testing conclusion from field planting shall prevail to find that no infringement of new plant variety rights has occurred.

Civil Ruling of the Supreme People's Court

(2015) Min Shen Zi No. 2633

Reapplying Applicant (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Shandong Denghai Pioneer Seed Co., Ltd. Domicile: Sanshandao Special Industrial Zone, Laizhou City, Shandong Province.

Legal Representative: Wu Shuke, Chairman of the Board of the company.

Agent ad litem: Ding Feng, lawyer of Beijing Guangdu Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Liu Shaohui, lawyer of Beijing Guangdu Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Shaanxi Nongfeng Seed Co., Ltd. Domicile: Room B138-139, Shaanxi Agricultural Means of Production Market, West Section of Beierhuan, Weiyang District, Xi'an City, Shaanxi Province.

Legal Representative: Zhao Yongqiang, General Manager of the company.

Agent ad litem: Zheng Xueyi, lawyer of Beijing Boren Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Shanxi Dafeng Seed Co., Ltd. Domicile: No. 49, Wucheng South Road, Xiaodian District, Taiyuan City, Shanxi Province.

Legal Representative: Niu Xiaoxiao, Chairman of the Board of the company.

Agent ad litem: Zheng Xueyi, lawyer of Beijing Boren Law Firm.

The reapplying applicant, Shandong Denghai Pioneer Seed Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Denghai Company), dissatisfied with the civil judgment (2015) Shan Min San Zhong Zi No. 1 rendered by the Shaanxi High People's Court in the case of dispute over infringement of new plant variety rights against the respondents Shaanxi Nongfeng Seed Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Nongfeng Seed) and Shanxi Dafeng Seed Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Dafeng Company), applied to this Court for retrial. This Court lawfully formed a collegial panel to review the case, which has now been concluded.

Denghai Company alleged in its application for retrial: (1) According to Article 2 of the Administrative Measures for DNA Fingerprint Identification of National Maize Variety Tests, which provides that the results of DNA fingerprint identification tests shall serve as the basis for the elimination, continued testing, and recommendation for approval of test varieties, and Article 9, which states that "if a test variety is found to have a minimal genetic difference from a known variety, i.e., identical or highly similar (number of differential loci ≤ 1), the test shall be stopped." The variety "Dafeng 30" had already undergone DNA fingerprint identification by the Maize Research Center of Beijing Academy of Agriculture and Forestry Sciences during its approval review in 2011, and the DNA fingerprint comparison between "Dafeng 30" and the known variety "Xianyu 335" showed 0 differential loci out of 40 loci. At that point, "Dafeng 30" should have been eliminated from the test varieties, withdrawn from the variety approval test, and disqualified from proceeding to DUS testing for further variety trials. The subsequent so-called "Report on Testing of New Plant Varieties" (hereinafter referred to as the DUS Test Report in question) should never have been produced, let alone be admitted as evidence. The DUS Test Report in question submitted by Dafeng Company is not legally valid. (2) The courts of first and second instance erred in characterizing DUS testing as field planting testing. There are significant differences between the two in terms of scope of application, criteria for determination, and specific content covered. DUS testing addresses whether a variety can be authorized and obtain protection as a new plant variety right, whereas field planting testing addresses whether a related variety is authentic. DUS tests specificity of a variety, while field planting tests authenticity. The determination standards for the two are vastly different. Specificity testing in DUS only examines a portion of the total traits of a variety, whereas field planting testing examines all traits. The courts of first and second instance treated the DUS Test Report in question as being equivalent to field planting testing for determining infringement of new plant variety rights, which lacks legal basis and constitutes an error in characterization. (3) Determining the authenticity of an organism is done by analyzing its genotype, not merely by observing its phenotype. "Dafeng 30" and "Xianyu 335" have identical DNA fingerprints. The courts of first and second instance mechanically judged based solely on a single phenotype, which is inconsistent with objective reality. Basing a judgment of non-infringement on the DUS Test Report in question is completely wrong. (4) "Dafeng 30" is not a variety lawfully bred by Dafeng Company itself. The "DNA Fingerprint Identification Report on Maize Varieties Dafeng 30, Xianyu 335 and Their Parent Materials" submitted by Dafeng Company lists the test materials as: A311 (female parent of Dafeng 30), PH6WC (female parent of Xianyu 335), PH4CV (common male parent of Dafeng 30 and Xianyu 335), Dafeng 30 (F1 hybrid), and Xianyu 335 (F1 hybrid). It is evident that the male parent used by Dafeng Company to produce "Dafeng 30" is PH4CV, the same male parent as that of "Xianyu 335". The public notice of the application for new plant variety rights for "Dafeng 30" submitted to the Ministry of Agriculture states: "this applied variety (Dafeng 30) is bred by crossing the self-selected inbred line A311 as female parent with PH4CV as male parent; the female parent A311 is developed by crossing Mo17 with PH6WC, then backcrossing with PH6WC for two generations, followed by two generations of self-pollination and selection." According to relevant literature, Mo17 is an inbred line developed in the United States in the 1970s. It was introduced into China when a Chinese agricultural and forestry delegation visited Canada in 1971, and a representative from the Beijing Academy of Agriculture and Forestry Sciences distributed seeds of the Mo17 inbred line to participants at the Northern Spring Maize Test Materials Exchange Conference in 1976. Based on genetic theory, the female parent of "Dafeng 30" is obtained by continuously backcrossing and transforming PH6WC, and the traits of the variety essentially reflect those of PH6WC, with almost no traits from Mo17. Therefore, from the perspective of genetic breeding, once Dafeng Company obtained both the male and female parents of "Xianyu 335", it effectively obtained the hybrid seeds of "Xianyu 335". The acts of Dafeng Company in producing and Nongfeng Seed in selling "Dafeng 30" constitute infringement of the new plant variety rights for "Xianyu 335." Denghai Company requests that this Court annul the judgments of first and second instance, conduct a retrial of this case, order Dafeng Company and Nongfeng Seed to immediately cease infringing the new plant variety rights for "Xianyu 335," and order them to compensate Denghai Company for economic losses in the amount of RMB 300,000.

Nongfeng Seed submitted a written opinion stating: (1) The test samples and sampling procedures in the DNA test report submitted by Denghai Company violated the regulations on crop seed inspection procedures, and therefore the samples are not legally valid as inspection evidence. (2) The DUS test report and other evidence submitted by Dafeng Company demonstrate that "Dafeng 30" is distinct from "Xianyu 335" and that "Dafeng 30" is a new maize variety with independent variety rights owned by Dafeng Company, which has been approved by the variety approval committee. Selling "Dafeng 30" under the authorization of the variety right holder is a lawful business activity and does not infringe upon the rights of any third party. (3) Denghai Company has not provided any evidence to prove that the alleged infringing product, packaged as "Dafeng 30" maize seeds, is in fact "Xianyu 335." During the first instance trial, Denghai Company explicitly stated that it would not apply for a judicial appraisal of whether the seized seeds in question were "Dafeng 30." During the second instance trial, because the seized seeds no longer existed, a judicial appraisal was impossible, and the consequence of failure to provide evidence should be borne by Denghai Company. Nongfeng Seed requests that this Court reject Denghai Company's application for retrial.

Dafeng Company's written opinion was identical to that of Nongfeng Seed, additionally submitting: (1) The DUS test conducted on "Dafeng 30" during the variety approval process was procedurally lawful and compliant. The first and second instance courts correctly affirmed the DUS Test Report in question. (2) "Dafeng 30" and "Xianyu 335" are two different hybrid varieties. The breeding method for the female parent A311 of "Dafeng 30" and the use of parent materials do not violate any legal provisions. Dafeng Company requests that this Court reject Denghai Company's application for retrial.

Upon review, this Court finds: Denghai Company filed the present lawsuit with the Xi'an Intermediate People's Court of Shaanxi Province on March 16, 2014, alleging that in 2013, Dafeng Company produced and Nongfeng Seed sold maize seeds packaged as "Dafeng 30," which infringed the new plant variety rights for "Xianyu 335." On June 9, 2013, the Beijing Maize Seed Testing Center tested the allegedly infringing seeds submitted for inspection. Using the DNA fingerprinting method for maize variety identification (NY/T1432-2007), with a 3730XL genetic analyzer and 384-well PCR instrument, the test result showed that the number of comparison loci between the test sample (No. YA2196) and the control sample (No. BGG253, "Xianyu 335") was 40, with 0 differential loci. The conclusion was "identical or extremely similar."

During the first instance trial, Denghai Company explicitly stated that it would not apply for a judicial appraisal of whether the seized seeds in question were "Dafeng 30."

"Dafeng 30" maize seeds were approved and promoted varieties by the Shanxi Province and Shaanxi Province Crop Variety Approval Committees in February 2012. The variety source of "Dafeng 30" is A311 x PH4CV.

The "Explanation on the Testing and Approval Situation of the 'Dafeng 30' Maize Variety" issued by the Shanxi Provincial Agricultural Seed Station on April 25, 2014, records: When "Dafeng 30" was submitted by Dafeng Company for variety approval in 2011, because the DNA fingerprint identification conducted by the Maize Research Center of Beijing Academy of Agriculture and Forestry Sciences found no differences between "Dafeng 30" and "Xianyu 335" across 40 comparison loci, the conclusion was that the two varieties had no significant differences, and "Dafeng 30" was not approved that year. Dafeng Company raised an objection. For this reason, the station in 2011 commissioned the Ministry of Agriculture New Plant Variety Testing Center to conduct a DUS test on "Dafeng 30" compared with "Xianyu 335." The conclusion was that "Dafeng 30" is distinct, uniform, and stable, and is a different variety from "Xianyu 335."

The DUS Test Report in question bears the seals of the Ministry of Agriculture New Plant Variety Testing (Yangling) Sub-Center and the Ministry of Agriculture New Plant Variety Testing Center, stamped on December 8, 2011, and December 26, 2011, respectively. The relevant content recorded therein is as follows: Material source: "Provided by the Ministry of Agriculture New Plant Variety Testing Center, via express mail, seeds received on March 10, 2011"; Test number: Jian 2011-001A; Variety name: Dafeng 30. Test location: Test Base of Yangling Sub-Center at the Third Agricultural Experiment Station of Northwest A&F University, Yangling, Shaanxi. Test period: "First growing cycle, April 25, 2011 – August 29, 2011." The experimental design records: "Sowed on April 25, 2011, by dibbling in opened furrows. The applied variety and the approximate variety were planted in adjacent rows, with 2 replications. Plot area: 16.4 square meters. Row length: 4.9 meters. Row spacing: 0.67 meters. Plant spacing: 0.35 meters. 15 plants per row after thinning. 4 rows per plot. 60 plants per plot. The standard variety was planted in 2 rows, totaling 30 plants, without replication." The specificity column records: "Approximate variety name: Jian 2011-001B Xianyu 335. Differing trait: 41* Ear: Intensity of anthocyanin coloration of glumes of cob. Description of applied variety: 8 strong to very strong. Description of approximate variety: 5 medium." The attached data results table records that, besides "41* Ear," the test results for Jian 2011-001A and Jian 2011-001B also differ in "9 Tassel: Intensity of anthocyanin coloration of anthers," which were "6 medium to strong, 7 strong"; "24.2* Plant: Height," which were "5 medium" and "7 high"; and "27.2* Ear: Length," which were "5 medium" and "3 short." The conclusion of the DUS Test Report in question is that "Dafeng 30" is distinct, uniform, and stable. The test standard used for the report is the "DUS Test Guide for New Plant Varieties – Maize" (2010) draft for approval.

During the second instance trial, Dafeng Company submitted a "DUS Test Report for Agricultural New Plant Varieties" dated January 23, 2014, bearing the seals of the Ministry of Agriculture New Plant Variety Testing (Yangling) Sub-Center and the Ministry of Agriculture New Plant Variety Protection Office. The test standard used for this report is the "Test Guide for Distinctness, Uniformity and Stability of New Plant Varieties: Maize" (2012 edition). The test report records that the test number was 2011-0819A, the test period covered two growing cycles: "April-August 2012, April-August 2013," the material source was provided by the Ministry of Agriculture New Plant Variety Testing Center, and the approximate variety was Xianyu 335. The report records the differing traits as: "11. Tassel: Intensity of anthocyanin coloration of anthers, applied variety: 7 strong, approximate variety: 6 medium to strong"; "41. Grain: Shape, applied variety: 5 wedge-shaped, approximate variety: 4 nearly wedge-shaped"; "42. Ear: Intensity of anthocyanin coloration of glumes of cob, applied variety: 9 very strong, approximate variety: 6 medium to strong." The test conclusion is that the variety is distinct, uniform, and stable. The "Examination Report on DUS of Agricultural New Plant Varieties" records: Application No. 20110059.3, variety name Dafeng 30, test number 2011-0819A, testing unit: Ministry of Agriculture New Plant Variety Testing (Yangling) Sub-Center, conclusion: distinct, uniform, and stable, review date: April 28, 2014.

The "A311" maize variety was granted new plant variety rights on September 1, 2015, with an application date of January 21, 2011, and a protection period of 15 years from the date of authorization. Dafeng Company is the variety rights holder. Dafeng Company applied for new plant variety protection for "Dafeng 30" on January 21, 2011, under Application No. 20110059.3, with a publication date of July 1, 2011, and Publication No. CNA007603E.

This Court holds that the focus of the dispute in this case is: whether the first and second instance judgments erred in finding that the alleged infringing maize seeds "Dafeng 30" produced by Dafeng Company and sold by Nongfeng Seed did not infringe the new plant variety rights for "Xianyu 335."

Regarding Denghai Company's assertion in its retrial application that the DUS Test Report in question submitted by Dafeng Company is not legally valid: Article 18 of the Seed Law of the People's Republic of China (2013 Amendment) (hereinafter referred to as the Seed Law) provides that "if a crop new variety or forest tree breed that has not passed approval is objected to by the applicant, the applicant may apply for a review to the original approval committee or the approval committee at the next higher level." Article 34 of the Measures for the Examination and Approval of Major Crop Varieties also provides that "if an applicant objects to the approval result, it may apply for a review to the original approval committee. If the variety approval committee office deems it necessary, it may arrange for one production cycle of variety testing before the review." Variety testing includes regional testing, production testing, and DUS testing. After Dafeng Company raised an objection to the DNA testing conclusion in the variety approval process for "Dafeng 30," the Shanxi Provincial Agricultural Seed Station commissioned the Ministry of Agriculture New Plant Variety Testing Center to conduct a DUS test. This does not violate the provisions of the above laws and regulations. The DUS Test Report in question was produced by the Ministry of Agriculture New Plant Variety Testing Center, which, in accordance with Article 16 of the Measures for the Examination and Approval of Major Crop Varieties — "DUS testing shall be organized and implemented by the Ministry of Agriculture New Plant Variety Testing Center" — designated the corresponding testing institution to accept the test materials and conduct field planting according to the test tasks. The test personnel carried out field trial design and testing, organized the test data according to the relevant test guide, described the traits, and compiled the test report, which was reviewed, signed, and sealed by the person in charge of the testing institution before being submitted to the testing center. The test report is truthful, lawful, and relevant to the facts to be proven in dispute. Denghai Company's assertion in its retrial application that the DUS Test Report in question is not legally valid lacks factual and legal basis, and this Court does not support it. This Court notes that the "Test Guide for Distinctness, Uniformity and Stability of New Plant Varieties: Maize" stipulates that the test period shall be at least two independent growing cycles, while the test report in question shows a test period of only one growing cycle: "April 25, 2011 – August 29, 2011." However, as Dafeng Company submitted during the second instance trial a "DUS Test Report for Agricultural New Plant Varieties" dated January 23, 2014, in which the test variety underwent two growing cycles and exhibited clear and reproducible differences in three traits compared to the approximate variety "Xianyu 335," this complies with the provisions of NY/T2232-2012 "Test Guide for Distinctness, Uniformity and Stability of New Plant Varieties: Maize" that "when the applied variety has obvious and reproducible differences from the approximate variety in at least one trait, the applied variety can be determined to be distinct." Therefore, the test report in question can be relied upon to determine that "Dafeng 30" is distinct.

Regarding Denghai Company's assertion in its retrial application that the DUS Test Report in question is not field planting testing: This Court holds that when conducting variety approval for major crops, the variety applying for approval must be clearly distinguishable from other varieties already approved or accepted by the variety approval committee at the same level. In 2011, during the application for variety approval of "Dafeng 30," because the DNA fingerprint test found no difference from "Xianyu 335," it was considered the same variety and failed to pass the year's variety approval. The main reason Dafeng Company objected to the DNA fingerprint test and applied for field planting testing was that the two varieties had obvious differences in traits and were different varieties. The DUS Test Report in question verified whether there were differences between "Dafeng 30" and "Xianyu 335" through field planting, and verified whether the two varieties were different through the characteristics and traits exhibited in field planting. Although the DUS test conducted was not for determining whether to grant new plant variety rights, the test content still involved whether the test variety "Dafeng 30" was distinct from the approximate variety "Xianyu 335." The differences in test tasks and test objects did not affect the breeding evaluation conducted under the same test standard. Denghai Company's assertion in its retrial application that the first and second instance courts erred in characterizing DUS testing as field planting testing is ambiguous in concept, and this Court does not support its argument that the DUS Test Report in question lacks probative value.

Regarding the grounds for retrial raised by Denghai Company that the DNA fingerprint identification conclusion established the existence of infringement, this Court holds that both the Seed Law of the PRC and the Regulations of the PRC on the Protection of New Plant Varieties (hereinafter "Regulations on the Protection of New Plant Varieties") provide that propagating material refers to seeds and other parts of a plant capable of reproducing the plant, including grains, fruits, and roots, stems, seedlings, buds, leaves, etc., and at the same time require that propagating material must possess novelty, distinctness, uniformity, and stability as prerequisites for granting the right to a new plant variety. The examination and approval authority for variety rights conducts substantive examination of the distinctness, uniformity, and stability of the applied variety based on field growing DUS testing. When approving major crop varieties, variety testing is also conducted based on the breeding report and comparative test report of the variety applied for approval, testing and analyzing and evaluating the traits exhibited by the variety in field cultivation. Therefore, for propagating material as a living organism, its characteristics and traits should be determined based on the trait characteristics identified through DUS testing conducted in field cultivation. DNA fingerprint technology, as a method for genotypic identity identification conducted indoors, is economical, convenient, not affected by the environment, and has a short testing period, which is conducive to timely protection of the rights holder's interests, and can also improve the efficiency of distinctness evaluation by screening similar varieties. In practice, it is often used to test the authenticity and uniformity of varieties, and fingerprint databases for relevant varieties have been constructed based on molecular marker technology. Since the core primers (loci) used in DNA testing do not necessarily correspond to the trait characteristics in DUS testing, and the authorization of a new plant variety is based on field growing DUS testing, when the DNA identification conclusion is identical or highly similar, a paired field DUS testing comparison can be conducted directly to determine identity through field phenotypes. Where the alleged infringing party claims that the conclusion of distinctness determined by field growing DUS testing should override the DNA fingerprint testing conclusion, it should provide evidence to prove this. Since the DUS testing report submitted by Dafeng Company proved through field cultivation that "Dafeng 30" possesses distinctness compared with "Xianyu 335", according to the rule for determining infringement of a new plant variety right that "the characteristics and traits of the allegedly infringing product are identical to those of the authorized variety, or the differences in characteristics and traits are not caused by non-genetic variation", the characteristics and traits of "Dafeng 30" and "Xianyu 335" are not identical, and there is no act of infringing the new plant variety right. Denghai Company's claim in its retrial application that the alleged lack of distinctness between "Dafeng 30" and "Xianyu 335" should be determined based on the DNA identification conclusion in this case is not supported by this Court. In this case, the seized allegedly infringing product was packaged as "Dafeng 30". Denghai Company did not apply for judicial identification to determine whether the contents were actually "Xianyu 335" sold under the "Dafeng 30" packaging (a practice known as "套牌经销" or "brand replacement distribution"). The courts of first and second instance, based on the DUS testing report in this case, found that "Dafeng 30" produced by Dafeng Company and sold by Nongfeng Seed Industry did not infringe the new plant variety right of "Xianyu 335". This finding was not improper. However, in the operative part of the judgment, the court of second instance relied on the "Understanding and Application of the Supreme People's Court's Several Provisions on Specific Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Disputes over Infringement of New Plant Variety Rights" to examine and determine this case, which was an improper application of law. This Court hereby corrects this.

Denghai Company further argues in its retrial application that the male parent of "Dafeng 30" uses PH4CV, the male parent of "Xianyu 335", and the female parent A311 is derived from PH6WC, the female parent of "Xianyu 335", with minor modifications by adding the public inbred line Mo17, and thus "Dafeng 30" constitutes an infringement of the new plant variety right of "Xianyu 335". This Court holds that, according to Article 6 of the Regulations on the Protection of New Plant Varieties and Article 2 of the Supreme People's Court's Several Provisions on Specific Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Disputes over Infringement of New Plant Variety Rights, without the permission of the variety right holder, producing or selling propagating material of the authorized variety for commercial purposes, or repeatedly using the propagating material of the authorized variety as the propagating material of another variety for commercial purposes, shall be deemed to infringe the new plant variety right. The male parent PH4CV used by Dafeng Company to produce "Dafeng 30" is the same as the male parent of "Xianyu 335". However, Denghai Company has not submitted evidence to prove that PH4CV is an authorized protected new plant variety. Using this male parent to combine with other inbred lines to cultivate a hybrid does not constitute infringement of a new plant variety right. Even if, as Denghai Company alleges, the female parent A311 of "Dafeng 30" was bred from PH6WC, the female parent of "Xianyu 335", and the public inbred line Mo17 obtained as a gift, A311 is no longer the same as PH6WC and has been granted protection as a new plant variety. As the variety right holder of the new plant variety A311, Dafeng Company not only enjoys the right to produce and sell this variety, but also the right to combine A311 with another parent to breed another variety, or to repeatedly use A311 with another variety to produce another variety. Dafeng Company's use of its own protected inbred line A311 as the female parent and the public inbred line male parent PH4CV to breed "Dafeng 30" does not constitute an infringement of the new plant variety right of "Xianyu 335". Denghai Company's claim that Dafeng Company's act of modifying the female parent through backcrossing and then combining it in the original combination constitutes infringement of a new plant variety right is not supported by this Court.

In conclusion, Denghai Company's application for retrial does not meet the circumstances set out in Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC. Pursuant to Article 204, Paragraph 1, of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, the ruling is as follows:

The application for retrial by Shandong Denghai Pioneer Seed Co., Ltd. is rejected.

Presiding Judge: Zhou Xiang

Judge: Qian Xiaohong

Acting Judge: Luo Xia

Clerk: Zhang Bo

December 11, 2015
